svg.text: SDH rainbow: why the poor sicken first

g.text: AGE · SEX · GENES (fixed!)
LIFESTYLE: food, smoke, drink, sex, exercise
COMMUNITY: family, friends, faith, neighbours
LIVING: housing, water, work, school, clinic, transport
STRUCTURE: economy, policy, NHIS, gender, power
DAHLGREN-WHITEHEAD (exam!): 5 layers, inside out — fixed → lifestyle → community
→ living conditions → structural forces. Nurses act on ALL: counsel lifestyle, mobilise
community, navigate living barriers, ADVOCATE structure (PRO-II!).
GRADIENT (Marmot!): each step down wealth/education = sicker + shorter lives — NOT just
poor-vs-rich but EVERY rung. Ghana: north vs south, rural vs urban, girl vs boy schooling,
kayayei vs office — gradients everywhere. Name them, never blame victims.
NURSE'S SDH SCREEN (ask!): money ("treatment affordable…?") · food ("meals daily…?") ·
housing ("rooms? water? toilet? smoke?") · work ("leave possible…?") · transport ("how far?
cost?") · school ("missed days…?") · safety ("safe at home…?") · NHIS ("card active…?").
ACT: dawn appointments (market women!) · drugs + food parcels · transport funds · NHIS
renewal help · referral letters (social welfare!) · community links (CHPS! churches!). Small
navigations, huge adherence — default is usually POVERTY, not defiance.
GENDER lens: women decide-last, pay-last, eat-last — involve husbands-kindly + empower
("your health feeds the family!") + screen abuse privately (PRO-I!). Girl-children: school
kept = health won — counsel fees-vs-future with parents.
MANTRA: "Don't blame the defaulter — map the rainbow, bridge the gap."
